title: Sales Order Derivation Diagnostic Playbook
principle: Use layers for diagnosis, not as a fake runtime sequence. Several mechanisms can run beside each other and can be triggered again after a change.

layers.title: Document context
layers.question: Which commercial context did the order start in?
layers.why: A different sales area or document type can select different procedures before item-level debugging even begins.

layers.title: Copied and inherited values
layers.question: Was the value copied from master data, a customer-material record, or a predecessor?
layers.why: The current master record is not proof that an existing reference chain should contain the same value.

layers.title: Assigned procedures and search engines
layers.question: Which procedure or rule engine owns this result?
layers.why: The word procedure is reused across SD, but the engines behind it are not the same.

layers.title: Runtime item and logistics decisions
layers.question: Which current item context produced the logistics result?
layers.why: A correct upstream value can still create a surprising downstream result when another input changes.

layers.title: Financial and communication consequences
layers.question: What commercial, financial, or communication control consumed the result?
layers.why: Do not correct a downstream posting or form when the wrong commercial context was created upstream.

layers.title: Redetermination boundary
layers.question: What event should keep the old value, and what should run again?
layers.why: Many difficult incidents are not wrong determination. They are wrong assumptions about redetermination.

cases.title: Payment terms look old after master-data change
cases.symptom: The payer master was changed, but a new order created with reference still shows the old payment terms.
cases.wrong_first_move: Change partner determination or billing configuration because the field looks stale.
proof_path: Confirm the order was created with reference
Inspect predecessor header payment terms
Compare the date of the master-data change
Create a controlled order without reference and compare the value
cases.lead_conclusion: The predecessor can intentionally carry the old business context. Master data describes today's default; it does not rewrite an existing reference chain.

cases.title: Manual plant change moves the customer promise
cases.symptom: A user changes the delivering plant and the shipping point, route, dates, or confirmed quantity no longer match the original order result.
cases.wrong_first_move: Fix route or ATP independently because those are the visible differences.
proof_path: Compare old and new plant
Re-run shipping-point inputs
Trace route inputs
Compare scheduling dates
Compare ATP context and confirmation
cases.lead_conclusion: Plant is an upstream logistics input. A manual override creates a new fulfillment context and downstream differences can be correct consequences.

cases.title: Inbound purchase order creates the wrong sales context
cases.symptom: An inbound B2B message reaches S/4HANA, but the resulting order uses an unexpected sales area or document type and then pricing or material rules differ.
cases.wrong_first_move: Debug pricing condition records before proving how the order context was selected.
proof_path: Capture the inbound identifiers and relevant message fields
Trace standard or flexible B2B context determination
Confirm sales area and document type
Only then compare the procedures selected by that context
cases.lead_conclusion: Integration mapping can decide the commercial world in which normal SD mechanisms run. A downstream difference can begin at message-to-context determination.

cases.title: The team debugs the wrong output framework
cases.symptom: A sales or billing document exists but no expected customer communication is produced.
cases.wrong_first_move: Open Output Parameter Determination or classic NAST configuration without first identifying which framework the application uses.
proof_path: Identify application and active output framework
Confirm output item or proposal creation
Trace rule or condition result
Confirm recipient and channel
Check form/render/send status
cases.lead_conclusion: S/4HANA Output Control and classic SD Output Determination have different rule paths. Framework identification is step zero.

cases.title: Product proposal is confused with cross-selling
cases.symptom: The business expects an additional product suggestion but configuration is changed in the wrong feature.
cases.wrong_first_move: Treat every product suggestion as the same SD mechanism.
proof_path: Identify the trigger
If customer and sales area drive the list, trace Dynamic Product Proposal
If an entered material drives complementary items, trace Cross-Selling
After acceptance, trace normal item checks
cases.lead_conclusion: Dynamic Product Proposal is customer-context driven; Cross-Selling is product-context driven. Both help entry, but they answer different questions.

cases.title: Revenue account is correct but profit center is wrong
cases.symptom: Billing posts to the expected G/L account, but profitability is assigned to an unexpected profit center.
cases.wrong_first_move: Change revenue account determination because both results appear in the same financial document.
proof_path: Separate G/L account determination from profit-center derivation
Check controlling object where relevant
Check product/material profit center
Check flexible sales derivation if used
Trace inheritance into billing and FI
cases.lead_conclusion: G/L account and profit center are separate financial derivations. One can be correct while the other is wrong.
